findings.summary: _inherited_entries reads the feedback index at pre-trim HEAD, but the carrier validates against the index at the replayed tip that _prepare trims to. If a prior generation crashed after its continuous review materialized (committing the artifact and appending an APPROVE entry) but before its receipt sealed, HEAD's index ends in APPROVE while the trimmed tip's does not, so new_attempt_is_legal declines a replay the carrier would have accepted -- and the generation re-dispatches a fresh implement against an already-satisfied spec, the BLOCKED jam this module exists to prevent. Reading `{tip}:.dev-dispatch/feedback/index.json` would match what the carrier sees. The tip index is always a prefix of HEAD's, so the error is conservative-only and never admits an illegal attempt.

The comment in test_a_fully_reviewed_chain_replays_through_to_acceptance claims the continuous- and final-review handoffs 'materialise alongside the replayed configure/implement'. They do not: both reviews are replayed, and dd_pipeline.py:402-431 returns the Replayed result before any materializer is consulted. The test's assertions check installed receipt bytes, not materialization. Spec requirement 5's 'continuous-review handoff materialization succeeds' clause is exercised only in test_the_implement_prefix_replays_and_the_review_runs_real and test_a_partial_prefix_replays_when_the_inherited_chain_ended_in_reject, and only against the fake Sealer -- the pinned plugin's carrier rule is never executed by any test.

new_attempt_is_legal's docstring says it is 'deliberately the same single source supervise/audit.py's chain check shares', but audit.py:40 imports only is_rework_link and rework_link_parent; this function has no second consumer. The rule is a hand restatement of the pinned plugin's check_chain_order with no conformance test, and the plugin is not vendored here, so drift is undetectable from this repo. Not a spec failure: the function is consulted only to decline a replay, never to admit one, so a stale mirror can only over-refuse.

Requirement 3 is satisfied for review-bearing candidates -- _final_replays (dd_replay.py:476) makes an APPROVE-final chain with a missing continuous intent replay through continuous review, final review and acceptance at generation 2, with a regression test that fails without the change. A prefix that still stops at implement (absent continuous receipt, broken digest link, both intents missing) is declined outright rather than continued, so its fresh continuous review would still be refused by the carrier. Recorded, not counted toward the verdict: continuing such a candidate would require either a new attempt (forbidden by requirement 1) or a fabricated review entry (forbidden by requirement 4), so fail-closed decline is the only reading that reconciles requirements 1, 3 and 4.

Product-tree identity between bb44376b and 95019d30 was not mechanically verified: this reviewer has only Read/Grep/Glob file inspection, so the mandated `git diff --exit-code ... ':(exclude).dev-dispatch'` was not executed and no shell or git command was run. File inspection shows only the reserved .dev-dispatch/ namespace carrying the rc-ef8ff40a artifact and the updated feedback index, with no sign of product drift -- consistent with a compliant metadata-only materialization. Separately, the committed implement handoff records work_head_commit 59751c0fc30dfe0a22f34c0f040529c70838b382 while the context supplies bb44376b as the product commit, consistent with a metadata-only implement materialization stacked on 59751c0f but unconfirmed against the object graph. The deterministic seal verifies HEAD independently; not counted toward the verdict.
